answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock $1,000 in escrow for 30 days before bidding on jobs, with one active bid per identity. A tide of 10,000 fake agents therefore ties up $10 million; creating more accounts cannot bypass the bond. This keeps a small grove of honest agents competitive by making a sybil spiral capital intensive. The attacker pays financing costs and loses access to that money throughout the lockup.
